clue.text: Defensive move by rugby player will get money from Ulster county

parts.note: to touch someone is to cadge money from them
Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A rugby player's defensive play is said to earn him cash from an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a player can touch the ball down behind his own goal line to defuse an attack. 'Touch' in British slang means getting money from someone ('he touched me for a fiver').
explanation.definitionFit: Grounding the ball in one's own in-goal area is a recognised defensive play in rugby.

clue.text: Last character has no, score — game off

parts.note: no score at all is nil, shown as the letter O

indicators.note: off suggests the word game going wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fails to score in a game that is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' in the surface sounds like a total of twenty, but here a nil score is the round letter, and 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet is the last character in that script.

indicators.note: spoilt tells us the words came in are damaged and their letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone came in and ruined the films.
explanation.definitionFit: Films collectively make up the art form of the pictures, the movies.

clue.text: Party 'turning blue? Try this amount of whisky

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of blue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party-goer turning blue is offered a large measure of whisky to try.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'do' is British slang for a party; the definition leans on 'Try', ordering a twice-sized measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A twice-sized measure of spirits is a common bar order.

parts.note: the rack is a torture device that stretches the victim

explanation.surface: A cowboy-style torture device is used to stretch seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrack is a name for coarse brown seaweed washed up on the shore.

clue.text: Darling, for example, this cheery hospital doctor

parts.note: light-hearted, so light means cheery
a houseman is a junior doctor resident in a hospital

explanation.surface: A dear, cheerful junior doctor on the wards is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is not an endearment but Grace Darling's family: her father William kept the Longstone lighthouse, and she famously rowed out to a wreck in 1838.
explanation.definitionFit: The Darlings of Longstone were keepers of a lighthouse off Northumberland.

parts.note: a scrap is a small fight, so a dealer in scraps would be a small-time warmonger; really the phrase means a dealer in waste metal

explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in waste metal is read as a trader in minor fights, scraps.

clue.text: If this cover is not in force, financiers rue the break-out

definitions.text: If this cover is not in force, financiers rue the break-out

indicators.note: a break-out shakes the letters of financiers rue loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Money men regret an outbreak of fire when their policy has lapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a 'break-out' of fire is what the financiers regret if their cover has lapsed, and 'break-out' also rearranges FINANCIERS RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy that pays out when property is burned is the cover whose lapse they would regret.

indicators.note: a drunk colonel is in disorder, so the letters of Col. Basset are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy army colonel named Basset is found in the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs to go with 'drunk', but it means barriers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bars are barriers or hindrances, things standing in the way.

clue.text: Making such deep sounds, Big Ben perhaps outstanding .

parts.note: Big Ben is the great bell in the Westminster clock tower
a debt that is outstanding is still owing

explanation.surface: Big Ben, an outstanding landmark, makes deep booming sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Roaring loudly in a deep voice is a description of the deep sound a bull makes.

clue.text: Black tea from Colombo — heat it thoroughly

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of the run of letters in Colombo and heat

explanation.surface: Black tea from Sri Lanka's capital should be heated right through.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea was once a name for a fine black tea grown in China's Wuyi hills.

parts.note: reads like a sailor below deck, but means the picture card found in a pack, or deck, of cards

explanation.definitionFit: The jack is the court card below the queen, also called by an older name meaning a rogue.

clue.text: This clue is numbered correctly for his 12

definitions.text: This clue is numbered correctly for his 12

parts.words: This clue is numbered correctly for his 12
parts.note: the clue's own number is 13, and a tradesman whose dozen is thirteen is the one famous for loaves

explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen, so for him '12' is counted as 13, the number this clue carries.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional bread-seller's dozen is thirteen loaves, matching this clue's number.

clue.text: Delivery of small thing about right at hospital

indicators.note: about means the small thing goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a bit is a small piece
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A tiny baby is delivered safely in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery in a maternity ward is a baby being born.

clue.text: Using skewered food,' king brings up infant

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up turns the word for infant upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a babe is an infant

explanation.surface: A king feeds his baby with food on a skewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings up' looks like raising a child, but turns BABE upwards into EBAB below K.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of meat grilled on a skewer are a classic Middle Eastern dish.

clue.text: At home, some sunshine about — but more likely to be this

indicators.note: about means the beam goes around the word for at home

parts.note: a ray is a beam, a little bit of sunshine
in means at home

explanation.surface: Staying home with a little sunshine around, though wet weather is more likely.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on the sunshine in the surface: the opposite, wet weather, is more likely.
explanation.definitionFit: The contrast with sunshine points to wet, showery weather.

clue.text: It backs a musical success inside part of South Pacific

indicators.note: inside shows the other pieces going within the turned-round word
backs means the word It is turned around

parts.note: a hit is a successful song

explanation.surface: A hit song is backed up inside part of the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: South Pacific is also a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: This French Polynesian island lies in the southern Pacific Ocean.

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word for layer is read in reverse

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: A creature is described as a backward stratum.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature of the non-human kind.

indicators.note: almost means the word for pet loses its last letter

parts.note: a rabbit is a common pet

explanation.surface: The teacher's favourite pupil is nearly there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'Teacher' is the definition and 'pet' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious leader's title literally means 'my master' or teacher.

definitions.meaning: a fish on the line has been landed
in cricket, one way a batsman is dismissed is when a fielder holds the ball

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman is 'out caught' when a fielder catches the hit ball before it lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a hooked fish and a batsman dismissed by a catch are taken this way.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Spare fight after midday (6)' for NARROW. ROW (fight) is clear, but 'midday' cannot supply NAR, so a word is misread or missing; no source found.

parts.note: a pet form, a shortened word, for the husband, the man of the house

explanation.definitionFit: A familiar shortened term for a husband is a diminutive of that word.

parts.note: to advocate a course is to urge it

indicators.note: without heart means the middle letter of not is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: An important lawyer is described as lacking compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advocate' looks like a lawyer but is a verb meaning urge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing that needs attention at once is important.

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of seat are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A broken railway seat makes someone cry out that it is bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like broken, but is the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is the upper chest, especially a woman's bosom.

clue.text: Help to provide seat for one standing

definitions.text: Help to provide seat for one standing

parts.words: Help to provide seat for one standing
parts.note: reads as giving a seat to someone on a crowded bus, but means voting a candidate into a parliamentary seat

explanation.definitionFit: Voters choose a candidate standing for office, giving them a seat.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Due to know (5)' for TOKEN. TO + KEN (know) is clear, but 'Due' is no definition of the answer; likely an OCR misread of a word such as 'Sign', not recoverable without a scan.

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
the Orpington is a breed of domestic chicken

explanation.surface: Something is pale and furious, rather like a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Livid' means angry in the surface but here means deathly pale. Orpington is also a London suburb, which disguises the chicken breed named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid can mean pallid, grey with shock, the colour of cinders.

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for tax reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A tax increase is shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like an increase, but turns TOLL upwards into LLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out is to distribute portions, to apportion.

parts.note: a wheeler might be a cyclist pedalling in reverse; really it means a person retreating from an earlier stance

explanation.definitionFit: Retreating from a stated position is like a cyclist pedalling in reverse.

definitions.meaning: to set up or establish, as in initiating proceedings

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to set up or begin; as a noun, an educational or learned body.
